text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — service=hosted-inference, severity=high, key=PD-87321. Auto-page to primary oncall.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy 'hosted-inference-critical' invoked. Primary did not ack in 2m, paging secondary. Escalation step: secondary + manager.

mike.sre: saw the page, jumping in. Investigating error spikes in logs now. Can someone confirm customer impact?

carol-support: customers reporting 503s for /v1/generate in EU region, around 1-5% of requests. Several payment flows retried. Support ticket volume up.

leah.eng: pulling metrics — p50 fine, p95 and p99 latency spiking, error rate from 0.3% -> 4.8% starting 02:12 UTC. Looks correlated to GPU pool autoscaler flapping.

mike.sre: thanks. Oncall note: primary hasn't acked, incident-bot shows second page at 02:15. I've started a quick mitigation: draining one suspicious host from the pool.

incident-bot: secondary ack by mike.sre at 02:16:34. Manager escalation fired to sre-manager at 02:16:40.

sre-manager: I'm on the bridge, joining now. Link: https://meet.company/incident/PD-87321

leah.eng: logs show repeated OOM traces from model runtime on host gpu-4, then connection pool exhaustion. Command I'm running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-4 && kubectl drain gpu-4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

mike.sre: cordon/drain executed, removing ~40% of in-flight connections from that host. Starting rolling restart of runtime on the node.

carol-support: temporary mitigation: routing set to prefer us-west for new traffic, TTL 30s. Not ideal but reduces error rate.

leah.eng: after drain, error rate dropped to ~0.8% in 3m. p95 back to normal for most tenants. Still seeing retries from a small customer cohort.

mike.sre: Confirmed. I'm going to stop autoscaler aggressive policy for the pool (scaleDownCooldown increased). Patch:```
PATCH /api/v1/runtime-config
Body: {"autoscaler": {"cpuThreshold": 0.65, "scaleDownCooldownSecs": 300}}
```
Applying now.

incident-bot: pagerduty-bot: secondary acknowledged, manager acknowledged. Escalation resolved: no further pages.

carol-support: Customer-impact summary for postmortem: brief error burst 02:12-02:22 UTC, peak affected requests ~4.8%, customers saw increased 5xx and automated retries. No data leakage.

sre-manager: Good mitigation. Immediate next steps: 1) run node-level diagnostics on gpu-4 (hardware vendor self-test), 2) adjust autoscaler rules to be less reactive for this pool, 3) add an alert for OOM patterns in runtime logs.

leah.eng: filing follow-up RFC for autoscaler fuzzy logic and adding KV cache backpressure metrics.

mike.sre: I'll own the post-incident runbook update for cordon/drain + autoscaler knobs. Posting timeline to pagerduty incident: https://pd.company/incident/PD-87321/timeline

carol-support: marking this incident as customer-impacting (P1) in support tool. Continuing to monitor; will escalate to product if SLA thresholds breached. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed by mike.sre at 02:48 UTC. Reminder: please file postmortem within 72 hours and include customer-facing summary.

sre-manager: Thanks team. Extra kudos for fast ack by secondary — prevented a wider outage. We'll review why primary missed the page (phone DND? app failure?) in the follow-up.

mike.sre: noted, will include primary paging telemetry in the report.

leah.eng: adding note: consider adding a short cool-down before autoscaler triggers when KV cache eviction rate is high.

carol-support: closing loop with customers: sending courtesy note and ETA for root cause follow-up.

pagerduty-bot: PD alert PD-87321 status -> closed.

mike.sre: final — archive logs and save snapshot of affected host before any vendor tests.

sre-manager: end of thread.
